name: Bladee
label: Trash Island
lede: A Stockholm painter's kid who turned Auto-Tune into a religion, and then, free of his label, made the album critics ranked No. 8 of 2024.

eras.title: A painter's kid from Skanstull
eras.text: Benjamin Reichwald grows up in Stockholm wanting to paint, and starts making noise with his classmate Zak Gaterud years before either of them is Bladee or Ecco2k.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bladee · The FADER: Being Bladee
years.h: Benjamin Thage Dag Reichwald is born in Stockholm
years.p: He grows up in the Skanstull area, the son of a teacher and a restaurant worker, and wants to be a painter.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia and the FADER, his mother was a schoolteacher and his father worked in restaurants. His younger brother Gus, later the videographer behind many Drain Gang and Sad Boys videos, is the one who put Yung Lean on his radar.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bladee · Wikipedia: Drain Gang · The FADER: Being Bladee
years.h: Krossad: a punk band with his classmate Ecco2k
years.p: Reichwald and [[Ecco2k|66ab36ce-8f58-46fb-9284-396c2c90ecbd]] start a band called Krossad, Swedish for "crushed", and put out a demo CD in 2007.
years.xp: Sources disagree on the details. Wikipedia dates Krossad to 2004 and the demo to 2007; the Drain Gang article calls it a grindcore duo from 2008; the FADER has him forming a punk band with Ecco2k at 11. Either way, the pair who later made Crest were already in a band together as kids.

eras.title: Gravity Boys
eras.text: Three Stockholm friends and a beatmaker pile onto SoundCloud, pick a name that keeps changing, and fall in next to Yung Lean's Sad Boys.

years.src: Wikipedia: Drain Gang · The FADER: Being Bladee
years.h: Gravity Boys Shield Gang becomes Drain Gang
years.p: [[Bladee|cd689e77-dfdd-4f81-b50c-5e5a3f5e38a4]], [[Ecco2k|66ab36ce-8f58-46fb-9284-396c2c90ecbd]], [[Thaiboy Digital|68d311c0-525f-4f72-a044-84e54565d02d]] and producer [[Whitearmor|984e5e75-e483-4670-ac53-9b5f28222437]] go through Gravity Boys and Shield Gang before landing on Drain Gang.
years.xp:
Bladee met Whitearmor and Thaiboy through mutual friends, and they started freestyling on Whitearmor's beats for fun. Wikipedia quotes him on the name: drain is about loss and gain, good or bad, and everything he and his friends do connects to that idea.

Their sound, sung through Auto-Tune over cold synths, fit the melancholy of Stockholm's Sad Boys, and the two crews fused.

years.h: Bladee's first guest spot: Yung Lean's "Heal You // Bladerunner"
years.p: The track on [[Yung Lean|757ed661-fbad-4e45-b1cd-a6b09f06f54a]]'s mixtape Unknown Death 2002 links Gravity Boys to Sad Boys for good.

years.h: Gluee, his first mixtape
years.p: Bladee's debut mixtape arrives in 2014, a summer-in-front-of-a-laptop record that Wikipedia calls an anthem for a suburban generation stuck scrolling Twitter.
years.xp: Wikipedia quotes that description of Gluee. It is the first full project under the Bladee name, with Whitearmor already in the production chair.

eras.title: Year0001 and a first album
eras.text: A Stockholm label signs the whole crew, Whitearmor builds Bladee's first real album, and a tour leaves one member at home for visa reasons.

years.h: Eversince: Bladee's debut album, all Whitearmor
years.p: Released through Year0001 and produced entirely by Whitearmor, with Ripsquadd and Hitkidd in support.
years.xp: Vice's Craig Jenkins heard modern rap, R&B, gothic and new wave in it; Gaffa's Jonathan Eklund called it a brilliant debut that stepped Bladee out of Yung Lean's shadow. Wikipedia notes it took years to reach physical formats: a Swedish CD in 2019, a US LP in 2022, a European LP in 2023.

years.h: All of Drain Gang sign to Year0001
years.p: The Stockholm label co-founded by Oskar Ekman and Emilio Fagone, Yung Lean's manager, becomes home for the whole crew.

years.src: Wikipedia: Drain Gang · The FADER: The album that sparked
years.h: Eversince Tour: Thaiboy Digital can't come
years.p: Bladee, [[Ecco2k|66ab36ce-8f58-46fb-9284-396c2c90ecbd]] and [[Whitearmor|984e5e75-e483-4670-ac53-9b5f28222437]] play their first major tour without Thaiboy, who can't enter the EU after his 2015 deportation from Sweden.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports Thaiboy Digital was deported from Sweden in 2015 over immigration issues, which kept him out of the tour. The FADER adds that the group's 2019 album Trash Island was recorded in Thailand because he couldn't return.

years.h: The fans who didn't get it
years.p: During the 2016 US election, Drain Gang picked up an alt-right following the members rejected.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the members reject right-wing and white supremacist ideologies. Writer Cassidy George of 032c put it this way: the group's suffering, specific to the internet age, "has bred a fandom encompassing the two most extreme poles" of politics. Later queer themes, notably in the 2020 video for "Amygdala", widened the audience.

years.src: Wikipedia: Working on Dying · Wikipedia: Bladee
years.h: Working on Dying with the Philadelphia producers
years.p: A mixtape made with the production collective of the same name, with Yung Lean and Ecco2k guesting.
years.xp: Working on Dying is the Philadelphia collective founded in 2012 by brothers F1lthy and Oogie Mane, known for a high-tempo 808 style. F1lthy would later do most of the production on Cold Visions.

eras.title: Struck by lightning
eras.text: Runways, a pop-up brand of cool, and a trip to Thailand that Bladee says changed how he saw everything.

years.h: Red Light and the single "Decay"
years.p: Whitearmor, Gud and Yung Sherman executive produce Bladee's second album.

years.src: WKNC: Bladee's Cold Visions · Wikipedia: Bladee
years.h: Icedancer, produced by Ripsquadd
years.p: A year-end mixtape with Yung Lean and Thaiboy Digital on it.
years.xp: Fans often group Icedancer with Working on Dying when they say Cold Visions feels like a return to form, as one WKNC critic put it.

years.big: "I was sure I was gonna die, but I didn't."
q: I was sure I was gonna die, but I didn't.
years.src: The FADER: Being Bladee · Wikipedia: Bladee
years.h: A lightning strike in Thailand
years.p: Bladee says he was hit by lightning on a trip to Thailand.
years.xp:
In the FADER's 2019 interview he said the strike made "everything make sense" and left him feeling like an angel. Wikipedia dates it to the 2019 Thailand trip and calls it transformative.

The same interview lays out the Trash Island worldview: the world is a trash island, and you have the power to create your own reality.

years.src: The FADER: The album that sparked · Wikipedia: Drain Gang
yt: Drain Gang live in NYC, full set
years.h: Trash Island, recorded in Thailand
years.p: Drain Gang's 22-minute, eight-track album, made in Thailand because Thaiboy Digital couldn't come back to Sweden.
years.xp: The FADER calls it the group's tightest project and the one that took them past cult status. Solo records followed fast: Thaiboy's Legendary Member two weeks later and Ecco2k's E two months after.

eras.title: Four albums in one pandemic year
eras.text: Bladee goes prolific: Gotland, a holy number, a Mechatok rave record, then the Drain Gang name starts turning up in Dazed and Rolling Stone.

years.h: Exeter: nine songs recorded in a week on Gotland
years.p: His first big run with producer Gud is 18 minutes 21 seconds long, the shortest Bladee album to date.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Ben Dandridge-Lemco gave it 7.2 and called it the sort of album that rewards leaning in, per Wikipedia. Anthony Fantano gave it a 5.

years.h: 333, a surprise drop three months later
years.p: Whitearmor executive produces the record named for Drain Gang's holy number, three.

years.h: Good Luck with Mechatok, and a Charli XCX remix
years.p: Bladee premieres the EDM-tinged Good Luck by livestream; the deluxe edition adds [[Charli XCX|260b6184-8828-48eb-945c-bc4cb6fc34ca]]'s remix of "Drama".

years.h: The Fool: pop rap, made with Lusi
years.p: Pitchfork's Nadine Smith gave it 7.7; The FADER ranked it No. 11 of 2021.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Lusi with most of the production and describes a turn toward introspection and spiritual questions. Dazed placed it 14th on its year-end list.

years.h: Real Sprin9: his solo show at Residence Gallery, London
years.p: The painter's kid gets a gallery exhibition through August.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Drain Gang Interview · Wikipedia: Bladee
yt: Drain Gang live at The Hollywood
years.h: Crest: Bladee and Ecco2k, all Whitearmor
years.p: The duo's joint album before a US tour with sold-out shows in Queens.
years.xp: Rolling Stone called it a soaring and rapturous triumph. Its piece on the first US Drain Gang tour describes rain falling on the crowd before the show and the room erupting like a blissed-out exorcism. Bladee: "We've never compromised on that."

years.h: Spiderr, the sixth solo album
years.p: Ecco2k directs the video; it follows Crest, and Wikipedia cites its mixed reception as part of the backdrop to Cold Visions.

eras.title: Cold Visions
eras.text: Skrillex, art shows and a record with Yung Lean, then a surprise album made alone in his Stockholm house that lands at No. 8 on Pitchfork's 2024 list.

years.h: Skrillex: "Real Spring" and "Ceremony"
years.p: Bladee lands singles with Skrillex, the second also with Yung Lean.

years.h: Psykos, a surprise album with Yung Lean
years.p: Palmistry and Silent$ky produce the 8-track, 22-minute World Affairs release.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it their first collaborative album after more than a decade working together, recorded across Thailand and Sweden. Pitchfork gave it 8.0 and The Needle Drop a 5.

years.src: Album of the Year: Cold Visions · Wikipedia: Cold Visions · WKNC: Bladee's Cold Visions
years.h: Cold Visions: 30 tracks dropped on a Tuesday night
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.3, Best New Music, and ranked it No. 8 of 2024; The FADER put it at No. 4.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Bladee made it in about two weeks at his house in Stockholm, in a depressive stretch as he approached 30, with the reception of Spiderr on his mind. Kieran Press-Reynolds' review, as quoted by AOTY and Wikipedia, called it "the most fully realized project of his career".

F1lthy handles most production, with Yung Lean, Yung Sherman, Thaiboy Digital and Black Kray appearing; Ecco2k does not. Wikipedia lists it as his first solo release outside Year0001.

years.h: "One Second" video, directed by Harmony Korine's EDGLRD
years.p: [[Yung Lean|757ed661-fbad-4e45-b1cd-a6b09f06f54a]] guests on the second single from Cold Visions.

yt: Bladee and Yung Lean, One Second (live)
years.h: Bladee and Yung Lean play "One Second" live at III Points
years.p: Live video of the song from the III Points festival.

years.big: "I don't owe them my next five projects."
q: A lot of stuff wasn't what we thought it was.
years.src: The FADER: Bladee discusses · Wikipedia: Drain Gang
years.h: Drain Gang leaves Year0001
years.p: Bladee, Ecco2k, Thaiboy Digital, Gud and Yung Lean part from the label in 2024.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the departure was announced that autumn. In a February 2025 FADER interview Bladee said that when they got a lawyer, "a lot of things were not in order or standard." He said he didn't owe Year0001 his next projects.

eras.title: Saint George
eras.text: Free of Year0001, Bladee puts out a three-song EP on his own label, tours ten countries and keeps the prolific run going.

years.h: Ste the Beautiful Martyr 1st Attempt, three tracks on Trash Island
years.p: A 7:47 surprise EP built around Saint George imagery.
years.xp: Kieran Press-Reynolds read the Saint George imagery as a fight against the evil things in Bladee's mind and called the opener "One in a Million" textbook Bladee. The video has him in a graveyard with a flag-wrapped sword.

years.h: The Martyr World Tour, his biggest yet
years.p: Announced in May across 10 countries, it starts in October 2025.

years.h: Sulfur Surfer, produced entirely by Whitearmor
years.p: His eleventh solo project, which Wikipedia says was inspired by ego death and the feeling of mid-transformation.
